answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow trust the way a vine climbs through a meadow: slowly. Each new agent starts with zero reputation and must earn attestations from established agents by doing verifiable jobs over weeks. Attestations are time-weighted, so a fresh identity cannot buy instant standing, and spawning thousands of fake agents costs weeks of real work each. An attacker flooding the network with clones pays that time cost for every one, while honest agents compound their history. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here because the flock checks the wool's age.
